seoTitle: Free Anchor Text Distribution Checker for Backlinks
metaDescription: Paste backlink anchor texts and see the share of branded, exact match, partial match, generic and URL anchors. Free, rule-based and runs in your browser.
intro: Paste a list of backlink anchor texts and see how they split into branded, exact-match, partial-match, generic and naked-URL buckets, with counts and percentages.
why:
A natural backlink profile contains mostly brand names, naked URLs and generic phrases such as "click here". A profile dominated by one exact money keyword is a classic sign of over-optimised link building, and worth checking during an audit or before a link campaign.

Export your anchors from your backlink tool, paste them here and set your brand terms and target keywords. Each anchor is sorted into a bucket by simple rules and you get a table with shares and bars. If exact-match anchors exceed about ten percent you get a warning. The rules are heuristics, not Google's rules, so use the result as a prompt for review.
howTo: Paste your anchor texts, one per line. Repeats are fine and count separately.
Enter your brand terms, separated by commas.
Enter your target keywords, separated by commas.
Read the bucket table and the warning about exact-match share.

faq.a: In order: a URL or bare domain is a naked link, a text containing a brand term is branded, an exact keyword is exact match, one that contains a keyword or one of its words is partial, and known phrases like "read more" are generic.

There is no official number. Most natural profiles are mainly branded and URL anchors, with few exact-match ones. The tool warns above about 10 percent exact match, which is a rule of thumb, not a Google threshold.

faq.q: Why do many anchors land in Other?
faq.a: Anything that matches no rule falls into Other, for instance an article title or a person's name. Add more brand terms or keywords, or review that bucket manually.
